blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — routine Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis
stem: An unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant client asks when Rho(D) immune globulin is routinely given. Which response is correct?

options.A: At 26 to 28 weeks of gestation and again postpartum if the newborn is Rh-positive.
options.B: At 12 to 14 weeks of gestation and again postpartum if the newborn is Rh-negative.
options.C: At 36 to 38 weeks of gestation and again postpartum if the maternal antibody screen is positive.
options.D: After delivery of an Rh-negative newborn when no antepartum prophylaxis was administered.

rationale: Current RhoGAM labeling recommends routine antepartum prophylaxis at 26 to 28 weeks of gestation for an appropriate unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant client. A postpartum dose is indicated when the newborn is Rh-positive and is administered within 72 hours of delivery. Therefore A is correct. B, C, and D use incorrect gestational timing, infant Rh status, or sensitization criteria.
educational_objective: State that routine Rho(D) immune globulin prophylaxis is given at 26 to 28 weeks of gestation and postpartum when the newborn is Rh-positive.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_locator: Indications and Usage §1.1; Dosage and Administration §2.1, Pregnancy and other obstetrical conditions: antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks and postpartum if newborn is Rh-positive, within 72 hours of delivery.
source_claim_supported: For an unsensitized Rh-negative pregnant client, routine antepartum RhoGAM prophylaxis is given at 26–28 weeks; postpartum prophylaxis is indicated when the newborn is Rh-positive and should be administered within 72 hours of delivery.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: review pertinent data prior to medication administration; educate client about medications; administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four timing choices to comparable lengths without absolute-word distractor cues.
Preserved one uniquely correct timing pattern anchored to current RhoGAM labeling.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the labeled routine antepartum and postpartum prophylaxis schedule; the revised distractors remove the prior absolute-word and length cues.
